A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The scientific material matches throughout; v2's additional page results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic-data OLS experiments, including approximation and refit results in Tables 1–3 and outlier diagnostics in Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original OLS simulation results in Section 4 and Appendix C, including numerical comparisons and additional failure-mode experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical AMIP, Additive One-Exact, additive one-step Newton, and greedy procedures. No algorithm component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated one-outlier, Simpson's paradox, poor-conditioning, and greedy-failure scenarios, including the modified data arrangements in Appendix C. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparisons involving AMIP, Additive 1sN, Greedy AMIP, and Greedy 1sN. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, generating distributions, outlier locations, removal fractions, and predicted-versus-refitted evaluation procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: The outlier diagnostics, additional greedy-failure examples, and modifications of the Simpson's paradox and poor-conditioning examples in Appendix C are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Reporting of point estimates and success/failure outcomes is unchanged. Neither version introduces different run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8 retain the same results. For example, Table 2 reports AMIP's refit estimate as 0.279 and both greedy methods' refit estimates as -0.990 in both versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: The optimization definitions, Taylor and one-step Newton derivations, Propositions C.1–C.2, and OLS approximation-error analysis in Appendices B–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about approximation failures in simple OLS settings, the same methodological contributions, and the same practical recommendations.

C2.justification: Explanations involving leverage, masking, and conditioning remain identical, as do qualifications concerning more complex models and the computational costs of greedy methods in Section 5 and Appendix D.

D1.justification: Simulation construction details and computational-cost descriptions are unchanged, and PDF hyperlink targets match. The expanded funding acknowledgment adds no implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Appendix A are unchanged. The bibliography reflows without adding, removing, or revising references.

P1.justification: v2 adds MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab as a second author affiliation and adds that lab and NSF TRIPODS award DMS-2022448 to the Section 6 funding acknowledgment. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added affiliation line and superscripts shift the abstract downward, while the longer acknowledgment reflows the bibliography onto an additional page. Figures and tables retain identical presentations; appendix pagination shifts by one page.

improvement.justification: v2 expands affiliation and funding disclosures, with minor associated layout changes. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, proofs, explanations, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so the administrative updates produce no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
